feasibility: 1 canonical records pass course-reference feasibility checks. Academic relevance is not assessed.
reviewStatus: Provisional academic finding. The trial schedules remain internal while the active record shows the supported external curriculum.
findings: The strongest feasible programme combines legal foundations and public and private branches with public economics, economic modelling, accounting, finance and research. Taxation and redistribution are real subjects within Public Economics, and international macroeconomics covers fiscal policy. No course evidence establishes a sustained sequence of fiscal statutory interpretation, tax liability, procedure or treaty allocation.
The commercial trial adds business organisation, governance and research. These strengthen the context for studying firms but do not teach how corporate or personal tax liabilities are determined.

The public-law trial studies state authority, rights, institutions and movements, with public economics. These supply substantive context for public revenue but do not establish the legal administration, dispute handling and cross-border tax rules that organise the bachelor. The limitation is academic and persists after the offering repairs. The present disposition remains open while the external curriculum entry condition is checked.
